prompt: A $95\%$ confidence interval for the mean weight of apples from an orchard is $(150, 162)$ grams. Which statement correctly interprets the confidence LEVEL of $95\%$?

choices.label: $95\%$ of the apples in the orchard weigh between 150 and 162 grams.
There is a $95\%$ probability that the true mean weight is between 150 and 162 grams.
If we took many random samples and built an interval from each, about $95\%$ of those intervals would capture the true mean weight.
$95\%$ of sample means would fall between 150 and 162 grams.

hint: The confidence level describes the METHOD over many repetitions, not this one interval or individual apples.

hints.text: The confidence level describes the METHOD over many repetitions, not this one interval or individual apples.
The true mean is a fixed number: it is either in $(150, 162)$ or it is not, so "95% probability" does not apply to this specific interval. And intervals are about the mean, not single apples.
C: in the long run, $95\%$ of intervals made this way capture the true mean.

explanation: A is about individual apples; a confidence interval says nothing about the spread of individuals.
B treats the true mean as random. It is fixed; the interval is what varies from sample to sample. D confuses the interval with the sampling distribution.
C is the textbook meaning: the method succeeds (captures $\mu$) in about $95\%$ of all possible samples.

alternativeExplanations.title: Level vs. interval
steps: Interpreting the INTERVAL: "We are 95% confident the true mean apple weight is between 150 and 162 g."
Interpreting the LEVEL: "The method captures the true mean in 95% of samples."
The question asks about the level, so C.
